We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse structure: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) meaning an aniline attached to carbonyl (amide) with NH attached to phenyl (anilide). Actually C(=O)N c3ccccc3N: carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl bearing an NH2? The SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N means amide nitrogen attached to phenyl which also has an NH (aniline). So product is N-phenyl-2-aminobenzamide? Anyway.

We need 3 steps retrosynthesis using given hints: step1: amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). step2: Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. step3: sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus forward direction: start from sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) + aniline (the amine) to give sulfonamide (aryl-sulfonamide). Then Doebner modification to create α,β-unsaturated acid attached to that phenyl? Actually Doebner forms α,β-unsaturated acid from aldehyde and malonic acid. So we need aldehyde precursor: aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde?) The target has a phenyl ring (the one attached to sulfonyl) bearing the α,β-unsaturated chain. So that phenyl ring must have an aldehyde at para position relative to sulfonyl? In target, the sulfonyl attached to phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). The chain /C=C/C(=O)N... is attached at para position relative to sulfonyl? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So the phenyl ring has the unsaturated amide at para position relative to sulfonyl. So we can start from that phenyl ring bearing sulfonyl and aldehyde at para position, then Doebner to give unsaturated acid, then amide coupling with aniline to give amide, then sulfonamide formation? Actually sulfonamide formation attaches sulfonyl to amine (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + aniline). In target, the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl sulfonyl and to the phenyl ring (the one with unsaturated chain). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to both sulfonyl and phenyl (aryl sulfonamide). So the amine used for sulfonamide formation is the phenyl ring (the one that later gets the unsaturated chain). So step order: first form sulfonamide between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the phenyl amine (aniline). That phenyl amine must have an aldehyde substituent that later undergoes Doebner to give unsaturated acid, then amide coupling with aniline (different aniline) to give final amide.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Gives precursor: α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl-sulfonamide (same as target but carboxylic acid instead of amide). Then disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid via Doebner (retro). Gives aldehyde phenyl-sulfonamide (para-aldehyde). Then disconnect sulfonamide to sulfonyl chloride + aniline (the phenyl-sulfonamide precursor). So three steps.
